content: 1. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction necessitates caution, close monitoring, or the use of an alternative drug. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative drug. If adverse effects occur, management may require dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation. Close monitoring is essential. 3. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for erythromycin-related adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 4. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for erythromycin-related adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Consider alternative therapy if necessary. 5. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate and nortriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate and olanzapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. Monitor closely. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If coadministration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects emerge, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 17. Erythromycin lactobionate and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid use in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant medications that prolong the QT interval, electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure, or bradyarrhythmias. 18. Osilodrostat and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Osimertinib and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of oxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Monitor closely. 21. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat is known to significantly prolong the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against use with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 31. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 35. Erythromycin lactobionate and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of penicillin G aqueous by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Monitor closely. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of penicillin VK by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 41. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 44. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Erythromycin lactobionate and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate increases pimozide levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of piperacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Monitor closely. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of pitavastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Do not exceed 1 mg/day of pitavastatin. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Ponatinib increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 55. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of pravastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely for toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status. 57. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
